title: Universal first-order thickening of an algebraic space over another
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A,A^{+},X$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Given $f:A\to X$, $i:A\to A^{+}$ and $f^{+}:A^{+}\to X$, say that $(i,f^{+})$ is a universal first-order thickening of $f$ if $i$ is a first-order thickening [def-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-data], $f^{+}\circ i=f$, and the following holds: for every pair of algebraic spaces $T,T^{+}$ over $S$, every first-order thickening $j:T\to T^{+}$, every $b:T^{+}\to X$ and every $a:T\to A$ satisfying $f\circ a=b\circ j$, there exists exactly one $a^{+}:T^{+}\to A^{+}$ such that $a^{+}\circ j=i\circ a$ and $f^{+}\circ a^{+}=b$. This is a predicate on the specified maps; it asserts no existence of universal thickenings.
